# Security framework coverage

<!-- Generated by `pnpm coverage:frameworks -- --write` from threats/*.yaml and threats/mappings/frameworks.yaml. Do not edit by hand: `pnpm coverage:frameworks` and the core test suite fail when this file is stale. -->

This matrix maps every shipped Singularity AIDR detection rule to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025, the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 and MITRE ATLAS (content release 2026.09). The mapping is data (`threats/mappings/frameworks.yaml`), keyed by rule id; a test fails when a rule has no mapping or uses an identifier that is not in the official lists.

A mapping means the rule detects an instance of that risk or technique where AIDR sees it: an agent's tool call (command, file path, URL, tool input) or a skill/plugin file. It is not a claim that every variant of the risk is prevented. The rules are patterns, and each item's rationale states what is and is not detected. Other AIDR components (DLP/privacy engine, MCP gateway, package reputation, behavioural analyzer) are named where they matter but are not counted here.

At runtime the matched rule's IDs travel with the verdict: `Verdict.frameworks` in TypeScript and `frameworks: {owasp_llm, owasp_agentic, mitre_atlas}` in local audit-log entries, SIEM incident exports (JSON, CEF, LEEF) and `aidr audit export`. Remote telemetry sends only `matched_threat_id`; the dashboard resolves the IDs from the mapping bundled at build time. `aidr coverage` prints this matrix from the rules installed with the CLI.

Rules evaluated: **428** active rules in **27** rule files.

Status meanings: **covered** - the rules address the item's attack surface at the agent's tool-call boundary; **partial** - some behaviours of the item are detected and the rationale names what is not; **not covered** - in scope for an agent guard but no rule addresses it; **not applicable** - the risk sits somewhere AIDR's rules cannot observe.

## OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025

Source: https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/

Summary: 3 covered, 5 partial, 0 not covered, 2 not applicable (of 10).

| ID | Title | Status | Rules | Example rules | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| LLM01:2025 | Prompt Injection | partial | 16 | LLM-IIN-001, LLM-IIN-002, LLM-IIN-003 | Pattern rules catch known direct and indirect injection phrasing, chat-template special tokens, jailbreak personas and instruction-hijack text inside skill files. They are regular expressions over tool inputs and plugin content: paraphrased, translated or novel injections are not reliably detected, and model-side input is not inspected by these rules. |
| LLM02:2025 | Sensitive Information Disclosure | covered | 82 | CLT-CMD-013, CLT-CMD-020, CLT-CMD-021 | For an agent's tool calls the rules cover the main disclosure paths: reading credential, key, cloud, keychain and browser stores, known API-key formats in commands or content, and exfiltration over HTTP, DNS, archives and cloud or code repositories. Personal data inside model responses is out of scope for these rules and is handled by the separate DLP/privacy engine. |
| LLM03:2025 | Supply Chain | partial | 50 | AISC-001, AISC-002, AISC-003 | Rules flag install-script piping, unpinned or unsigned package installs, miner packages, insecure dependency sources and malicious skill/plugin content. For models, downloads from Hugging Face organisations or hosts outside the trusted model sources, weight downloads over plain HTTP, trust_remote_code and unsafe model deserialization are held or denied. Model files are not verified by hash or signature, dataset provenance is not checked, and package reputation needs the separately deployed package-check endpoint (inert when none is configured). |
| LLM04:2025 | Data and Model Poisoning | partial | 6 | AISC-001, AISC-002, AISC-003 | AIDR sits at the agent's tool-call boundary and never sees training, fine-tuning or embedding data, so poisoned data and backdoored weights are not detected. What the rules do catch is the loading step through which a tampered model file runs code: torch.load without weights_only, pickle/joblib/dill on downloads, Keras safe_mode=False and numpy allow_pickle=True in code the agent writes or runs. A poisoned model in a data-only format (for example .safetensors) passes. Runtime memory and context poisoning of an agent is tracked under ASI06. |
| LLM05:2025 | Improper Output Handling | covered | 94 | CLT-CMD-001, CLT-CMD-002, CLT-CMD-003 | Model-generated commands and code are validated before they execute: pipe-to-shell, reverse shells, eval of decoded payloads, LOLBin and script-host execution and obfuscated command lines are denied or held for approval at the tool boundary. Code the agent writes is also checked by the secure-code guardrails (eval or shell commands built from input, SQL built by string formatting, TLS verification off, permissive CORS, exposed debuggers, CSRF off, weak crypto); those are language-gated patterns over added lines and warn by default rather than block. Output rendered in a UI (XSS, markdown links) is not covered by these rules. |
| LLM06:2025 | Excessive Agency | covered | 306 | CLT-CANARY-001, CLT-CMD-001, CLT-CMD-002 | The rule set is primarily an excessive-agency control: destructive deletion, persistence, privilege changes, security-control tampering, credential access and discovery performed through the agent's tools are denied or require out-of-band human approval. |
| LLM07:2025 | System Prompt Leakage | partial | 3 | LLM-SPE-001, LLM-SPE-002, LLM-SPE-003 | Three rules flag system-prompt extraction requests (direct, repetition and translation tricks) in tool inputs. Leakage through model output and indirect extraction phrasing outside those patterns are not detected. |
| LLM08:2025 | Vector and Embedding Weaknesses | not applicable | 0 | - | AIDR does not operate a retrieval pipeline, vector store or embedding service, so there is nothing for a tool-call rule to inspect for this risk. |
| LLM09:2025 | Misinformation | not applicable | 0 | - | Detection rules judge what an agent does, not whether model output is true. Hallucinated-package risk is partly addressed by the separate package-reputation check, not by these rules. |
| LLM10:2025 | Unbounded Consumption | partial | 17 | CLT-MINE-001, CLT-MINE-002, CLT-MINE-003 | Cryptominer binaries, pools, wallets and miner flags launched through an agent are blocked (compute hijacking). Token, request-rate and cost exhaustion of the model API itself are outside what these rules observe. |

## OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026

Source: https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/

Summary: 3 covered, 5 partial, 2 not covered, 0 not applicable (of 10).

| ID | Title | Status | Rules | Example rules | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| ASI01:2026 | Agent Goal Hijack | partial | 14 | LLM-IIN-001, LLM-IIN-002, LLM-IIN-003 | Injection, triggered-instruction and hidden-instruction patterns in tool inputs and skill files are detected. Goal hijack that uses ordinary wording, or that only shows up as a changed plan, is not visible to pattern rules; the resulting harmful tool calls are still caught by the ASI02/ASI05 rules. |
| ASI02:2026 | Tool Misuse and Exploitation | covered | 310 | CLT-CMD-001, CLT-CMD-002, CLT-CMD-003 | This is the enforcement point of the product: every rule evaluates a tool call (shell command, file path, URL or tool input) before it runs, and dangerous uses of legitimate tools are denied or held for out-of-band approval. |
| ASI03:2026 | Identity and Privilege Abuse | covered | 101 | CLT-CMD-012, CLT-CMD-014, CLT-CRED-001 | Credential dumping, credential-store and key access, alternate-credential execution, sudo/UAC abuse, account creation and group changes, and access to AIDR's own approval key are detected. Delegated agent identity (tokens issued to the agent) is verified by the delegated-credential feature, not by these rules. |
| ASI04:2026 | Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities | partial | 49 | AISC-001, AISC-002, AISC-003 | Skill and plugin packages are scanned for injected instructions, remote payloads, embedded code, credential exfiltration and insecure dependencies, and risky install commands are flagged. Models from untrusted Hugging Face organisations or hosts, plain-HTTP weight downloads, trust_remote_code and unsafe model loading are held or denied. MCP server identity and signed manifests are enforced by the MCP gateway rather than these rules; model integrity (hash or signature) and dataset provenance are not covered. |
| ASI05:2026 | Unexpected Code Execution (RCE) | covered | 118 | AISC-001, AISC-002, AISC-003 | Download-and-execute chains, pipe-to-shell, reverse shells, encoded or obfuscated execution, script hosts and LOLBins on Linux, macOS and Windows are denied before the command runs. Loading model files through code-executing deserializers and trust_remote_code are held or denied, and eval, shell commands built from input and network-exposed debuggers in code the agent writes are flagged by the (advisory) secure-code guardrails. |
| ASI06:2026 | Memory & Context Poisoning | partial | 4 | LLM-MEM-001, LLM-MEM-002, SKILL-T02-001 | Content that asks the agent to persist instructions in memory, and skill files that write into agent memory or instruction files, are flagged. Poisoning through ordinary-looking stored content or retrieval data is not detected. |
| ASI07:2026 | Insecure Inter-Agent Communication | not covered | 0 | - | No rule inspects agent-to-agent messages or protocols (A2A, shared task queues). MCP traffic is inspected by the MCP gateway, which is a separate component. |
| ASI08:2026 | Cascading Failures | not covered | 0 | - | Rules act on single tool calls on one host; they do not model failure propagation across agents or workflows. Blocking a harmful call limits blast radius but is not claimed as coverage of this risk. |
| ASI09:2026 | Human-Agent Trust Exploitation | partial | 4 | CLT-SELF-005, CLT-SELF-007, SKILL-T01-002 | Rules flag skills that tell the agent to hide actions from the user and agent attempts to forge or self-issue the human approval AIDR requires. Persuasive or misleading agent output shown to a human is not analysed. |
| ASI10:2026 | Rogue Agents | partial | 60 | CLT-CANARY-001, CLT-MAC-CMD-013, CLT-MAC-CMD-015 | Behaviour typical of a compromised or rogue agent is detected: tampering with or disabling AIDR itself, reading or changing AIDR's canary credentials, disabling OS security controls, clearing logs and hiding artifacts. Slow behavioural drift within allowed actions is not something a per-call rule can see (the behavioural analyzer is a separate, optional detector). |

## MITRE ATLAS 2026.09

Source: https://atlas.mitre.org/

Summary: 34 of 208 techniques/sub-techniques mapped (9 covered, 25 partial); 13 of 16 tactics touched.

| ID | Title | Status | Rules | Example rules | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| AML.T0010.003 | Model | partial | 14 | AISC-001, AISC-002, AISC-003 | The routes by which a compromised model reaches the agent's host are flagged: downloads from Hugging Face organisations or hosts outside the trusted model sources, weight downloads over plain HTTP, remote model code and code-executing model formats. A compromised model from a trusted publisher, or tampered weights in a data-only format, are not detected; files are not verified by hash or signature. |
| AML.T0010.005 | AI Agent Tool | partial | 26 | SKILL-T01-001, SKILL-T01-002, SKILL-T01-003 | Skill and plugin packages are scanned before use against the T01-T09 skill risk taxonomy. Compromise of a remotely hosted tool that changes after the scan is not visible. |
| AML.T0011 | User Execution | partial | 4 | AISC-005, AISC-006, AISC-007 | Enabling trust_remote_code (in code or on a serving command line), which runs Python shipped in a model repository, is held for approval and denied for publishers outside the trusted model sources. |
| AML.T0011.000 | Unsafe AI Artifacts | partial | 7 | AISC-001, AISC-002, AISC-003 | Loading unsafe AI artifacts is held or denied: torch.load without weights_only, pickle/joblib/dill on downloaded files or network responses, Keras safe_mode=False, numpy allow_pickle=True and unsafe YAML loaders. The Python patterns apply to code the agent writes or runs; a loader reached through a library wrapper the patterns do not name is missed. |
| AML.T0011.001 | Malicious Package | partial | 3 | CLT-MAC-SUPPLY-002, CLT-MINE-015, CLT-MINE-016 | Installs of known miner packages and unsigned remote installer packages are flagged. |
| AML.T0012 | Valid Accounts | partial | 1 | CLT-WIN-CMD-025 | Running commands under alternate user credentials (runas) is held for approval. |
| AML.T0025 | Exfiltration via Cyber Means | covered | 8 | CLT-CMD-013, CLT-CMD-020, CLT-CMD-021 | Sensitive-file upload, DNS-label exfiltration, alternative protocols, automated exfiltration tooling and transfers to code repositories or cloud storage are detected. |
| AML.T0048.000 | Financial Harm | partial | 17 | CLT-MINE-001, CLT-MINE-002, CLT-MINE-003 | Cryptomining through an agent (a direct financial harm to the victim) is blocked; other financial harms are out of scope. |
| AML.T0050 | Command and Scripting Interpreter | covered | 85 | CLT-CMD-001, CLT-CMD-002, CLT-CMD-003 | Shell, PowerShell, AppleScript/JXA, Python and script-host execution patterns used for remote payloads, obfuscation and proxy execution are detected across all three OSes. |
| AML.T0051 | LLM Prompt Injection | partial | 5 | LLM-INJ-001, LLM-INJ-002, LLM-INJ-003 | Known injection and jailbreak phrasing only; see OWASP LLM01. |
| AML.T0051.001 | Indirect | partial | 5 | LLM-IIN-001, LLM-IIN-002, LLM-IIN-003 | Indirect-injection phrasing in tool content and instruction-hijack text in skills is detected; unseen wording is not. |
| AML.T0053 | AI Agent Tool Invocation | covered | 346 | CLT-CANARY-001, CLT-CMD-001, CLT-CMD-002 | Every tool call the agent makes is evaluated against the rules before it executes; a hijacked agent's tool invocations are the input AIDR inspects. |
| AML.T0054 | LLM Jailbreak | partial | 2 | LLM-INJ-002, LLM-INJ-003 | Known jailbreak personas and tokens (DAN, developer mode) are detected. |

| AML.T0056 | Extract LLM System Prompt | partial | 3 | LLM-SPE-001, LLM-SPE-002, LLM-SPE-003 | Three system-prompt extraction patterns; see OWASP LLM07. |
